Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

µ-MATH · dataset size: µ-MATH is a solution-judgment meta-evaluation dataset of 1,084 labeled samples drawn from 271 U-MATH problems, rather than another spelling of U-MATH’s 1,100 problem-solving tasks.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.mu-math.distinct-units.v3

  • The retained family IDs remain distinct despite inconsistent umath/mumath link spellings inside the cards.
  • These are documented release units; no payload recount was performed.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

µ-MATH · labeled: For µ-MATH construction, the v4 paper describes four model-generated solutions per selected text-only problem, formal answer-equivalence checks through Gradarius-API, and in-house expert labeling of solutions receiving negative API responses.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.mu-math.labeling.v2

  • A negative API response is not itself treated as a wrong solution because extraction and expression conversion can fail.
  • The paper names Llama-3.1 8B among the four generators; the pinned creator card names Llama-3.1 70B. That source discrepancy is unresolved and neither size is silently substituted.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

µ-MATH · evaluates: µ-MATH evaluates a judge given a problem statement, reference answer and candidate solution as a binary correctness classifier, with macro-averaged F1 as its primary metric and positive/negative predictive values and true-positive/true-negative rates as secondary metrics.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.mu-math.metrics.v2

  • These are method definitions, not performance rankings or new experimental measurements.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

µ-MATH · filtered: The µ-MATH paper describes selecting 271 U-MATH problems using expert estimates of evaluation difficulty and explicitly states that the resulting set is not intended to reflect the overall U-MATH distribution.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.mu-math.sampling-limit.v3

  • The meta-evaluation sample is text-only and selected for judging difficulty; it does not establish judge quality for U-MATH visual problems or all university mathematics.
